root_cause.text: The `dev_fwd_path()` helper in `net/core/dev.c` used a `WARN_ON_ONCE()` on `stack->num_paths >= NET_DEVICE_PATH_STACK_MAX`, so when forwarding path resolution built an unusually long `net_device_path_stack` (made more likely by IPIP tunnels), the code could hit the warning condition instead of silently handling the overflow case.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `if (WARN_ON_ONCE(k >= NET_DEVICE_PATH_STACK_MAX))` to `if (k >= NET_DEVICE_PATH_STACK_MAX)`, and the commit message says “recent support for IPIP tunnels increases chances of reaching this WARN_ON_ONCE if userspace manages to build a sufficiently long forward path,” with the fix tied to `dev_fwd_path()` in `net/core/dev.c`.

intent_record.how: At runtime, the function still prevents writing past the end of stack->path by returning NULL when the path index is out of range, but it no longer emits a warning message when that limit is exceeded.
